newsitem.title: UK: P&O says no prospect of paying Florida fines.
newsitem.headline: P&O says no prospect of paying Florida fines.

text.p: Peninsular & Oriental Steam Navigation Co Plc said on Thursday there was "no prospect" of it paying fines in respect to allegations of unfair trading practices in Florida.
Earlier its share price had tumbled on a report in Lloyd's List newspaper said the company faced a U.S. lawsuit by the State of Florida over Government fees and port charges.
The stock was down 22-1/2 pence at 618 by 1010 GMT.

Lloyd's List said that the State of Florida sought fines of up to $15,000 against P&O's Princess Cruises unit for each passenger boarded at state ports over the last four years. It said the total size of any possible fines was not known.
It said Florida attorney-general Bob Butterworth said Princess had been "pocketing" money collected as port charges that customers were led to believe was a government fee.
But P&O says it is not prepared to concede on the matter.
"Other companies have settled with the Attorney General's office without admitting liability," it said in a statement.

"Their only penalty was reimbursement of the state cost of the probe. Princess could also have settled, and indeed could do so today, but such is the strength of our case that we were not prepared to concede the principle".
The lawsuit was first reported on Wednesday, when Florida said the fees added as much as $150 to advertised ticket prices.
"By keeping portions of these add-on fees for itself, Princess was able to advertise lower cruise prices than would otherwise be possible," Butterworth said.
Princess responded by the charges had no merit and that Florida had never detailed any violation committed by Princess.
"We believe that our advertising in the state of Florida had always communicated to consumers the full price of the cruise...," the company said in a statement.
"It could be hugely damaging to P&O," said the head of equity trading at one brokerage.
